passage: The final point came as the last light faded and the first raindrops hit the kabaddi ground. Kamal's team had won by a single raid. He punched the air, roared, and was swallowed by teammates hugging him and thumping his back. It felt wonderful, like something huge had lifted off his chest. Then he saw Rukmini, the rival captain, standing alone with her hands on her knees, soaked and not looking up. He heard himself stop shouting. With the rain coming harder and the crowd already heading for shelter, he walked across the wet mud and held out his hand. "That was the toughest match we've had. You were brilliant." She shook it, smiling a little.

qa.q: What happened as the last light faded?
qa.a: The first raindrops hit the kabaddi ground as Kamal's team won by a single raid.

qa.q: What was Kamal feeling when he saw Rukmini standing alone?
qa.a: He was still full of joy, but noticing her disappointment made him stop shouting and feel some care for her.

qa.q: Why was crossing the muddy ground to shake her hand a good choice?
qa.a: It shared his triumph graciously and avoided gloating, which could have hurt Rukmini more.

qa.q: How might Rukmini have felt when Kamal offered his hand?
qa.a: She was probably disappointed about losing, but touched by the respect, and her small smile suggests some comfort.

grounding: A teen cheers and hugs teammates after a win and shares the triumph graciously with the rival.

passage: "Yes! Yes! Three-two!" Abhinav yelled across the school quad, arms raised, as his house team stormed him in a heap. The inter-house football win was the best afternoon of his year. He jumped on a bench, pointed at the losing side and sang, "Who's the champion now?" A few of his teammates laughed. Then he saw Irfan, his friend since Class 6, sitting on the grass with his shirt pulled over his knees, staring at nothing. Abhinav's chest felt suddenly heavy. He climbed down, walked over and sat beside him. "That last goal was lucky," he said. "Your defence was really strong. Sorry about the singing." Irfan shrugged, but he moved over to make room.

qa.q: What was the score of the football match?
qa.a: The score was three-two.

qa.q: What was Abhinav feeling when he saw Irfan sitting on the grass?
qa.a: His joy was mixed with regret and concern, and his heavy chest suggests he realised his gloating had hurt a friend.

qa.q: What could Abhinav do after sitting down to keep the friendship strong?
qa.a: He could keep listening, avoid further gloating, and maybe suggest a friendly match later, showing that the friendship matters more than the win.

qa.q: How might Irfan have felt while Abhinav sang on the bench?
qa.a: He may have felt stung and small, since the song was aimed at his team, though he left room on the grass for Abhinav afterwards.

grounding: A teen celebrates a win with fist pumps and hugs, and learns that gloating can hurt while sharing it graciously helps.

passage:
"CHECKMATE!" Sachin slammed the rook down, jumped up and pumped his fist. "Yes! Yes! District champion!"
Across the board, the boy from the other school stared at his pieces, blinking hard.
Sachin turned to his teammate. "Ramesh, did you see? Too easy! He didn't even see it coming!"
Ramesh grabbed his sleeve. "Bhai. Look at him."
Sachin looked. The boy was quietly packing his pieces, his lip trembling. His father stood behind him.
Sachin's grin wobbled. "I didn't mean..."
"You won. Enjoy it. Just not on top of him."
Sachin took a breath. He walked back to the table and held out his hand. "That was a really hard game. Your knight move in the middle almost had me."
The boy looked up, surprised, and shook it. "Thanks. Well played."
Then Sachin ran outside and screamed with Ramesh behind the auditorium.

qa.q: What piece did Sachin slam down for checkmate?
qa.a: The rook.

qa.q: What was Sachin feeling right after the checkmate?
qa.a: Sachin felt triumphant and thrilled, pumping his fist after becoming district champion.

qa.q: What did Ramesh do that helped Sachin win graciously?
qa.a: He pointed out the other boy's upset and reminded Sachin to enjoy the win without gloating over him.

qa.q: How might the losing boy have felt when Sachin said "Too easy"?
qa.a: He probably felt humiliated and hurt, already upset about losing the final.

grounding: The dialogue shows a teenager's triumph after a win, and a teammate helping him share it graciously instead of gloating.

passage:
When our team won the inter-school debate last year, I felt like I could fly. The judges announced it and I actually jumped out of my chair. We hugged, screamed, took a hundred photos.
That part was fine. The part I regret came later. In the big group chat with both schools, I posted, "Imagine losing to US 😂 Shalini's team needs a new topic."
Within a minute, Shalini left the group.
I didn't think about how it would feel to be her, reading that after preparing for weeks. I only thought about how good I felt.
Next day I messaged her privately: "That was a nasty message. You argued really well on the second point. I'm sorry." She replied, "Thanks. It stung."
Now when I win, I celebrate with my team, and I say one kind true thing to the other side.
- Rashmi

qa.q: What did Shalini do within a minute of the message?
qa.a: Shalini left the group.

qa.q: What was Rashmi feeling when the win was announced?
qa.a: Rashmi felt triumphant and elated, as if able to fly, jumping up and celebrating.

qa.q: What does Rashmi do now after a win?
qa.a: Rashmi celebrates with the team and says one kind, true thing to the other side, instead of gloating.

qa.q: How did Shalini feel reading the gloating message?
qa.a: Shalini felt hurt and stung after weeks of preparation, which is why she left the group.

grounding: The account shows a teenager's triumph turning into gloating that hurts others, and learning to share wins graciously.

passage:
Coach's note - Kalyani, girls' kabaddi, Sunday
Our under-16 team won the zonal final today by two points. When the whistle went, the girls exploded: screaming, jumping, piling on top of Indu, who scored the last raid.
I let them. Triumph like that is earned.
What I want to record is what Indu did next. While the others were still dancing and chanting our school's name, she untangled herself and walked across the mat to the other team. Some of their players were sitting on the ground, crying. Indu shook each hand and said something to their captain I couldn't hear.
Later I asked her. She said, "I told her their defence was the best we'd played all year. It was."
Two of our girls had started chanting a rude line about the losing school. Indu turned round and waved them quiet.
I'm proud of the win. I'm prouder of that.

qa.q: By how many points did the team win?
qa.a: By two points.

qa.q: What was Indu feeling after scoring the last raid?
qa.a: Indu was triumphant and joyful, celebrating under the pile of teammates.

qa.q: What did Indu do that showed graciousness?
qa.a: She crossed the mat to shake every hand, praised the other captain's defence honestly, and quieted teammates who chanted a rude line.

qa.q: How might the losing team have felt when Indu came over?
qa.a: They were upset, some crying, but may have felt respected and a little comforted by her honest praise.

grounding: The coach's note shows teenagers celebrating triumph and one player sharing it graciously instead of gloating.

passage:
Saturday night
WE WON. Inter-school quiz final, 180 to 175, on the very last question. When Yash buzzed and said "Tungabhadra" and the quizmaster said "Correct!", I screamed, actually screamed, pumped both fists, and we hugged in a big sweaty heap on the stage. My cheeks hurt from grinning. Then I did a not-great thing. The St Mark's team had been smug all day, and their captain had said "good luck, you'll need it" in the morning. So I looked right at her and mouthed "need it?" with my eyebrows up. Everyone on our side laughed. And then I saw she was blinking really fast, trying not to cry in front of the whole hall. My stomach dropped. I walked over, shook her hand and said, "Closest final ever. Your team was brilliant on the science round." She said thanks, still wobbly. Yash said, "Vidya, that was the right thing." Still grinning though. 180!

qa.q: What was the final score?
qa.a: The final score was 180 to 175.

qa.q: What was Vidya feeling after mouthing 'need it?'
qa.a: Vidya was triumphant and a bit smug at first, then felt a sinking guilt on seeing the captain blinking back tears.

qa.q: How did Vidya turn the moment around?
qa.a: Vidya walked over, shook the captain's hand and praised the science round, sharing the win graciously instead of gloating.

qa.q: What was the win like for the St Mark's captain?
qa.a: For the captain it was a painful loss made worse by being mocked in front of the hall, so she was close to tears.

grounding: It shows a teenager's fist-pumping triumph after a win, a moment of gloating that hurts a rival, and the win then being shared graciously.
